title: Using a queue: taking turns
summary: Three programs share one CPU. Each runs for 2 time units, then goes to the back of the queue.

checkpoints.text: P0, P1 and P2 are waiting in the queue, in that order. They need 5, 2 and 3 units of time.
P0 got its turn: 2 units. It still needs 3 more.
P0 is not finished, so it joins the back of the queue, behind P1 and P2.
P1 needed only 2 units, so it finishes in its first turn and does not come back.
Every program got a fair share in turn: P0, P1, P2, P0, P2, P0. Operating systems schedule programs this way (round robin), using a queue.
